main.result_summary:
The 2002-01-24 consolidation is committed on `main` as one commit (`sleep: 2002-01-24 consolidation`). I haven't pushed it; the runner does that after its checks. Lint and sleep-audit are both green. The audit was red on the first try: six topic files had grown more than the 150-character limit. I shortened the new lines and moved two more out-of-date lines to the archive, and the second run passed. All 43 noted messages from 2002-W04 (m11145–m11265) are cited in 13 existing topic files plus one new person file, so `dataset/drops/sleep-120.tsv` is empty. The week's main items:
- Ken Lay resigned and the all-employee meeting was postponed.
- The FBI is searching the Enron Building; the owner sent orgcharts to Rob Walls and to the FBI, and copied the record-retention memos to AOL.
- The Research Library handover has to finish within a week.
- Recommendation letters are being written for Supatgiat, Ganjoo and Cope.
- He accepted a CERAWeek invitation as Michael Maddox's guest, and new recruiters approached him.

Michael Levy reached five messages, so he has a new person file and is in the alias table. Following the approval gates, I added a question about attaching the spelling "Michael N. Levy" to it rather than doing it myself. The "Raymond Bowen, Jr." question passed its due date unanswered, so I closed it as status quo with a (?) note in `memory/people/ray-bowen.md`. Four other open questions now point to the archive files their lines moved to. The five oldest still-open lines all remain valid. No file was above 90% of its size limit, so the compression quota had nothing to act on; seven files ended smaller than they started. `state.md` and the organization, industry, personal and people indexes are refreshed. Last week's run log and this week's four mail logs are in `memory/archive/inbox/`, and this run's log is in `memory/inbox/2002-01-24--run.md`. There was no sleep task, which is logged as a `(sleep-task-result)` line.
